records.segregation: Linked to 1p markers; cumulative multipoint lod score 3.69 at D1S244
quotes: we performed linkage analysis of two Japanese CMT2 families using markers flanking the CMT2A, CMT2B, and CMT2D loci. The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.

The clinical features of the CMT2A affecting the two families include similar levels of muscle weakness of the posterior and anterior tibial muscles, tendon reflexes preserved in upper extremities but reduced or absent in lower extremities, no enlargement of the peripheral nerves, and mild sensory disturbance in only 20% of affected individuals.

notes.statement: By exome sequencing of 33 CMT2/neuropathy-related genes, including MFN2, in 2 independent pedigrees of hereditary neuropathy diagnosed at the Neuromuscular Clinic of the Penn State Hershey Medical Center and Hamburg Center, Xu et al. (2018) identified a heterozygous a3260g transition in the KIF1B gene, resulting in a tyr1087-to-cys (Y1087C) substitution in KIF1Bbeta. The in silico programs PP2 and SIFT indicated that this was the only variant among the 33 genes with disease-causing capacity.
quotes: Coincidentally, we identified two hereditary neuropathy pedigrees carrying the same KIF1Bβ mutation Y1087C (Fig. 5, A and B; Table 1) by exome sequencing of 33 CMT2/neuropathy-related genes (Table 2). According to the in silico pathogenicity evaluation programs PP2 and SIFT, this KIF1Bβ mutation was the only one with disease-causing capacity in the single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within these 33 genes including MFN2.

we detected the a3260g (Y1087C) mutation of human Kif1bβ gene in the patients from two independent pedigrees of hereditary neuropathy suffering from CMT2A symptoms including progressive muscle weakness and slight central nervous system defects
Two new independent pedigrees of CMT2A were diagnosed at the Neuromuscular Clinic of the Penn State Hershey Medical Center and Hamburg Center.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) reported that the KIF1B Y1087C mutation was heterozygous, at chr1:10387567, with autosomal dominant inheritance and a 1000 Genomes minor allele frequency of 0.0395.
quotes: Confirmed mutation | KIF1B | CHR1: 10387567 | Y1087C | Heterozygote | Autosomal dominant | 0.0395

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) showed that the receptor tyrosine kinase IGF1R is a direct binding partner of KIF1Bbeta, binding through the intracellular domain of IGF1Rbeta to a minimal region spanning residues 885-1,410 of the KIF1Bbeta stalk domain, as demonstrated by yeast 2-hybrid analysis, vesicle immunoprecipitation from Kif1bbeta-EGFP knockin mouse brain, Nycodenz vesicle coflotation, GST pulldown of purified proteins, and comigration live imaging at about 1 micrometer/s.
quotes: Using the ICD of IGF1Rβ as the prey, blue colonies indicating a positive signal were successfully formed with the indicated bait fragments of the mouse KIF1Bβ stalk domain (Fig. 2 A). The binding domain of KIF1Bβ was thus minimized to 885–1,410 aa.

In this study, we first identified the association of IGF1R with KIF1Bβ using yeast two-hybrid, vesicle IP, coflotation, pulldown assay, and comigration experiments, and we also detected impairments in the surface presentation of IGF1R in Kif1b−/− neuronal axons, suggesting that IGF1R is a novel cargo of KIF1Bβ.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) found by GST pulldown of mouse brain lysates that the Y1087C mutation, which lies in the middle of the IGF1R minimal binding sequence, significantly decreased the binding capacity of the KIF1Bbeta 885-1,410-aa fragment to both IGF1R subunits, whereas binding to the synaptic vesicle precursor protein synaptophysin and to the adaptor DENN/MADD was unaltered.
quotes: The mutated KIF1Bβ 885–1,410 aa (Y1087C) fragment tended to exhibit a lower binding capacity to both of the IGF1R subunits than WT KIF1Bβ 885–1,410 aa. However, the binding capacities to the synaptic vesicle precursor protein synaptophysin and the adaptor protein DENN/MADD were likely unaltered by the Y1087C mutation (Fig. 5, C and D).
Note that the binding capacity to IGF1R but not that to DENN/MADD or synaptophysin was significantly decreased by the mutation.

notes.statement: In rescue experiments in Kif1b-null mouse hippocampal neurons, Xu et al. (2018) found that wildtype mouse KIF1Bbeta restored axonal outgrowth and axonal surface IGF1R expression, whereas KIF1Bbeta-Y1087C, KIF1Bbeta-Q98L, KIF1Balpha, and KIF1A significantly failed to complement; neurons expressing Y1087C also showed significantly reduced pAkt levels along the axon upon IGF-I stimulation.
quotes: Transfection of mouse WT KIF1Bβ restored axonal outgrowth. However, transfection of KIF1Bβ-Y1087C and KIF1Bβ-Q98L mutants, KIF1Bα, and KIF1A significantly failed in this complementation capacity compared with the WT KIF1Bβ, while KIF1Bβ-Y1087C could partially rescue it (Fig. 6 A).
Besides, the neurons expressing KIF1Bβ-Y1087C also showed a significant reduction in pAkt levels, whereas KIF1Bβ-WT successfully rescued this reduction.

The overexpression of mouse KIF1Bβ significantly rescued the axonal IGF1R expression level compared with control, while other constructs had lesser capacity for this complementation, similar with the case of axonal outgrowth above (Fig. 7, A and B).

notes.statement: By live imaging in Kif1b-null hippocampal neurons, Xu et al. (2018) found that the number of anterogradely transported IGF1R-containing vesicles was rescued by wildtype KIF1Bbeta but not by KIF1Bbeta-Y1087C, and that the ratio of comigrating to total KIF1Bbeta vesicles was significantly reduced with Y1087C, while motor velocity was unaffected; the authors concluded that the mutation is at least responsible for increasing susceptibility to neuropathies by reducing IGF-I signal transduction.
quotes: As a result, the number of transported IGF1R-containing vesicles was not rescued in the neurons expressing KIF1Bβ-Y1087C, whereas it was rescued in the neurons expressing WT (Fig. 8 D).

However, the ratio of comigrating over total KIF1Bβ-containing vesicles was significantly reduced in the neurons expressing Y1087C (Fig. 8 G). These results suggested that Y1087C could not gain the sufficient affinity to IGF1R. Thus, KIF1Bβ-Y1087C failed in transporting IGF1R to the axon.
Our in vitro evidence suggested that this mutation is at least responsible for increasing susceptibility to neuropathies by reducing the IGF-I signal transduction.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) found that axonal outgrowth was significantly impaired in dissociated hippocampal neurons of Kif1b-null mice at DIV2-3, and knockdown experiments with isoform-specific miRNA vectors showed that the beta isoform of KIF1B was specifically responsible; TUNEL staining showed that neurite-bearing Kif1b-null neurons were not largely apoptotic, although the overall apoptosis rate was higher than in wildtype.
quotes: We found that axonal outgrowth was significantly impaired in Kif1b−/− neurons at DIV2–3 (Fig. 1, A and B). In the knockdown experiments using the KIF1Bα- and -β–specific miRNA vectors, we found that the β-isoform of KIF1B was specifically responsible for this impairment in axonal outgrowth

Using terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick-end labeling (TUNEL) staining of dissociated hippocampal neuron culture at DIV3, we found that neurite-bearing Kif1b−/− neurons were not largely apoptotic, excluding the nonspecific effect of apoptosis as the cause of the axonal elongation phenotype (Fig. 1 F).

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) found that surface and axonal IGF1R levels were significantly decreased in Kif1b-null mouse hippocampal and cortical neurons by surface immunocytochemistry, microfluidic chamber axonal staining, and surface biotinylation, and that Kif1b-null neurons were insensitive to IGF-I stimulation of axonal elongation, with impaired IGF-I-induced increases in pAkt and pERK; constitutively active Ras V12 significantly rescued the axonal outgrowth deficit.
quotes: The IGF1R level in the cell surface fraction of Kif1b−/− neurons was significantly lower than that of Kif1b+/+ neurons (Fig. 3 E).

As expected, Kif1b−/− neurons were insensitive to IGF-I, and no significant axonal elongation was observed, whereas Kif1b+/+ neurons treated with IGF-I successfully developed the axons (Fig. 3, G and H).

Kif1b−/− neurons transfected with constitutively active Ras V12, which is upstream to the PI3K–Akt and ERK signaling (Castellano and Downward, 2011; Tanaka et al., 2016), showed a significant increase of the axon length compared with the Kif1b−/− neurons at DIV3 (Fig. 4, E and F).

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) transfected Kif1b+/+, Kif1b+/-, and Kif1b-/- hippocampal neurons with SP-IGF1Rbeta-RFP and found that Kif1b+/- neurons showed less anterograde IGF1R transport than wildtype neurons, with little transport observed in Kif1b-/- neurons, indicating that IGF1R requires KIF1Bbeta to be transported down the axon.
quotes: Kif1b+/− neurons showed less transport than Kif1b+/+ neurons (Fig. S2, G–J). Furthermore, little transport was observed in Kif1b−/− neurons. These data indicate that IGF1R requires KIF1Bβ to be transported down the axon.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) noted that IGF1R did not bind the corresponding stalk region of KIF1A (mouse KIF1A 836-1,346 aa), which shares 65% sequence identity with mouse KIF1Bbeta 885-1,410 aa, and found a nonconserved 20-aa stretch just before the core-binding residue Tyr1087; by superresolution microscopy, DENN/MADD and IGF1R scarcely colocalized, indicating that IGF1R is transported independently of synaptic vesicle precursors.
quotes: However, mouse KIF1A 836–1,346 aa, which was homologous to mouse KIF1Bβ 885–1,410 aa, did not result in blue colony formation (Fig. S2, A and B), suggesting that IGF1Rβ specifically binds to KIF1Bβ instead of KIF1A. The stalk domain of KIF1Bβ shares a high homology with the corresponding domain of KIF1A, with a sequence identity of 65%.
DENN/MADD and IGF1R scarcely colocalized with each other (Fig. 5, E–G).

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) noted that although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A, only a few pedigrees with KIF1Bbeta mutation for CMT2A1 had been reported, whereas MFN2 mutations are responsible for the most common known axonal form, CMT2A2; MFN2 and more than 30 related genes were intact in the authors' newly identified CMT2A pedigrees.
quotes: Although a KIF1B mutation in the same genomic interval was the first identified in a pedigree with CMT2A, only a few pedigrees with KIF1Bβ mutation for CMT2A1 have been reported until recently.

There are several pedigrees of CMT2A with MFN2 point mutations (Züchner et al., 2004; Kijima et al., 2005; Lawson et al., 2005; Baloh et al., 2007); however, MFN2 as well as >30 related genes were intact in our newly identified CMT2A pedigrees.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2018) noted that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, also known as hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy, is one of the most common inherited peripheral neuropathies with a prevalence of 1:2,500, and is divided into demyelinating CMT1 with nerve conduction velocity less than 38 m/s and axonal CMT2 with nerve conduction velocities greater than 38 m/s.
quotes: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease is one of the most common inherited peripheral neuropathies, with a prevalence of 1:2,500 (Skre, 1974) as the result of summing up the mutations in >30 genes (Saporta et al., 2011); this condition is also known as hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy.
Demyelinating CMT1 has a nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s, and axonal CMT2 has nerve conduction velocities >38 m/s.

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) found that Kif1b knockout mice died at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects, and death of knockout neurons in culture could be rescued by expression of the beta isoform. Kif1b heterozygous mice had a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and developed progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.
quotes: KIF1B knockout mice die at birth from apnea due to nervous system defects. Death of knockout neurons in culture can be rescued by expression of the beta isoform.
The KIF1B heterozygotes have a defect in transporting synaptic vesicle precursors and suffer from progressive muscle weakness similar to human neuropathies.

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) described an isoform of the kinesin motor KIF1B, KIF1Bbeta, which differs from the mitochondria-transporting KIF1B in its cargo-binding domain.
quotes: The kinesin superfamily motor protein KIF1B has been shown to transport mitochondria. Here, we describe an isoform of KIF1B, KIF1Bbeta, that is distinct from KIF1B in its cargo binding domain.

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2001) concluded that their findings clearly indicated that defects in axonal transport due to a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.
quotes: This is clear indication that defects in axonal transport due to a mutated motor protein can underlie human peripheral neuropathy.

notes.statement: In 2 Japanese families with CMT2, Saito et al. (1997) found linkage to chromosome 1p, with a highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 at D1S244. They excluded the CMT2B and CMT2D loci using markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.
quotes: The highest cumulative multipoint lod score of 3.69 was obtained at D1S244.
The CMT2B and CMT2D loci were excluded by the results of linkage analysis performed using markers D3S1551, D3S1290, and D7S484.

notes.statement: By linkage analysis in 6 large autosomal dominant CMT2 families, Ben Othmane et al. (1993) demonstrated linkage to microsatellite markers (D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228, D1S199) in the distal short arm of chromosome 1. Multipoint analysis of the linked families placed the CMT2A gene most likely within the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228 (odds approximately 70:1 of lying within versus outside the interval).
quotes: We have performed pedigree linkage analysis in six large autosomal dominant CMT2 families and have demonstrated linkage and heterogeneity to a series of microsatellites (D1S160, D1S170, D1S244, D1S228 and D1S199) in the distal region of the short arm of chromosome 1.

Multipoint analysis examining the "linked" families showed that the most favored location for the CMT2A gene is within the interval flanked by D1S244 and D1S228 (odds approximately 70:1 of lying within versus outside that interval).

notes.statement: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) found significant evidence for genetic heterogeneity by admixture analysis; only 3 of 6 CMT2 families (DUK662, DUK1241, 1523) had high posterior probabilities of linkage to 1p, suggesting that the CMT2 phenotype results from at least 2 different genes.
quotes: Significant evidence for heterogeneity was found using admixture analysis and the two-point lod scores.
These findings suggest that the CMT2 phenotype is secondary to at least two different genes and demonstrate further heterogeneity in the CMT phenotype.

notes.statement: Ben Othmane et al. (1993) described CMT2 as an inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by variable age of onset and normal or slightly diminished nerve conduction velocity, pathologically and genetically distinct from CMT1.
quotes: Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease type 2 (CMT2) is an inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by variable age of onset and normal or slightly diminished nerve conduction velocity. CMT2 is pathologically and genetically distinct from CMT type 1 (CMT1).

notes.statement: Hentati et al. (1992) studied 2 CMT2 pedigrees and excluded the CMT2 locus from the CMT1A region on chromosome 17 (lod score -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58). They also excluded it from the CMT1B region on chromosome 1 (lod score -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61). In the same study, a CMT1 pedigree showed linkage to the CMT1A region (lod score +3.67 at theta = 0.00).
quotes: we were able to exclude the CMT2 disease locus from the region of chromosome 17 (Z = -2.80 at theta = 0.05 for D17S58) where the CMT1A gene maps (Z = +3.67 at theta = 0.00)
negative lod score values were obtained in CMT2 for the region of chromosome 1 where the CMT1B gene has been located (Z = -3.09 at theta = 0.05 for D1S61)

notes.statement: Hentati et al. (1992) concluded that the hypertrophic (CMT1) and neuronal (CMT2) forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease are genetically heterogeneous. They found that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped at that time.
quotes: The present study therefore provides evidence for genetic heterogeneity between the hypertrophic and the neuronal forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and demonstrates that the CMT2 gene is not allelic to either of the CMT1 genes mapped to date.
